description_full: Bora Pharmaceuticals Co., LTD. engages in contract development, manufacture, and sale of pharmaceuticals in Europe, the United States, Taiwan, and internationally. The company operates through Sales, CDMO, and Other segments. It manufactures and sells generic, brand, and over the counter (OTC) drugs. The company also offers contract development and manufacturing services and technical services for the development of pharmaceutical products. In addition, it provides Western pharmaceuticals, including central nervous system medications, antibiotics, and gastrointestinal medications; and nutritional and vitamin supplements, physical recovery, and health care products. The company sells its products directly to clinics, pharmacies, pharmacy chains, and drug stores, as well as through distributors to medical centers, corporate and public hospitals, and regional and district hospitals. Bora Pharmaceuticals Co., LTD. was incorporated in 2007 and is based in Taipei City, Taiwan.

financial_summary: Bora Pharmaceuticals Co., Ltd. is a small-cap healthcare business with a $318M market cap on $578M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +20% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 17% against a 8% cost of capital, a 9-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it, with gross margins sitting at 43%.

The business throws off $106M in free cash flow — roughly 18 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.51× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 3.0× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and interest coverage runs at 6.8×.

Management returns a meaningful 13.6% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and within its sector the business captures 2.0× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
